scope: Bulk-dump vtable[8] (slot offset 0x20) of all Application::Main::Element::* subclasses (and base RaptureElement) to enumerate the Pattern B async dispatch tier. Closes the chapter opened by the map-tick-handler pass, the fun-0058cca0-caller-tree pass, the actor-map-writers pass, and the fun-004d9910-callers-map pass.

method.step1: RTTI enumeration: ran FindSymbolByName.java with BAHAMUT_SYMBOL_QUERY=Element::vftable LIMIT=500. Got 156 total Element::vftable matches across all namespaces.
method.step2: Filtered to Application::Main::* prefix (excluding Application::Main::SqwtInterface). 49 vtable VAs across 23 distinct classes (each class has primary + secondary vtable due to MI under RaptureElement).
method.step3: Read 4-byte function pointers at vtable_va+0x20 directly from the PE binary (tools/extractors/read_vtable8.py) - bypasses Ghidra round-trip and works for both primary and secondary vtables (DumpVtableSlots only returns the first vtable found for a class name).
method.step4: Histogrammed slot-8 targets: 14 distinct, with two dominant defaults (FUN_0091C520 n=23 primary subobject, FUN_00A72A20 n=13 secondary subobject no-op) and 10 per-class implementations + 2 shared mini-helpers.
method.step5: Decomped all 13 unique slot-8 functions via DumpFunctionDecomp.java (BAHAMUT_DECOMP_VAS list).
method.step6: Classified by structure: opcode-switch dispatchers (10) vs no-op stubs (3 - FUN_0055C250 BootupElement, FUN_0068E550 LightElement, FUN_00A72A20 RelativeElement/DaemonElement/XamlElement/FormElement/ClientWorkElement/CustomControlElement/CommonResourceElement/MainElement/TargetElement-tertiary/WidgetElement-tertiary/EffectDebugElement/DebugInfoElement secondary).

key_findings: Pattern B async tier mirrors sync tier structure: secondary vtable (the MI base subobject for non-RaptureElement classes) hosts the opcode-switch implementation; primary vtable's slot 8 is a shared base-class helper (FUN_0091C520) not opcode dispatch.
10 Element subclasses have per-class opcode-switch slot-8 dispatchers; 13 share defaults (no-op or stub).
CharaElement::vftable_secondary[8] = FUN_0058E0C0 (1519 bytes, 17 cases: 0x4A,0x4E,0x4F,0x50,0x51,0x53..0x61,0x64) - the largest async opcode dispatcher.
MapLayoutElement::vftable_secondary[8] = FUN_0059E660 (69 bytes, 8 cases: 0x22..0x28,0x2B,0x2C) - matches the per-class pattern of vtable[9] (FUN_0059CED0) being Map-specific too.

CutManagerElement::vftable_secondary[8] = FUN_00566740 (275 bytes, 10 cases: 4..0xD) - cutscene async events; confirms the existence of Application::Main::Element::System::CutManagerElement that an earlier attempt was hunting (that attempt had failed mid-batch with API Overloaded).
GameManagerElement, CameraElement, ScreenshotManagerElement, SqwtElement, EffectElement each have small (1-4 case) per-class slot-8 dispatchers.

Pattern B participant count is 23 Application::Main::Element classes (1 base RaptureElement + 22 derived), NOT 27 as previously estimated in client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns'. That finding needs to be corrected.

The fun-0058cca0-caller-tree pass's prior count of 27 likely conflated MI-secondary vtables (each class has 2: primary + secondary, with TargetElement having 3 and WidgetElement having 4) with distinct classes.

The case values in slot-8 functions (e.g., CharaElement cases 0x4A..0x64) do NOT match Actor cluster s2c opcodes (0xCC..0xE5). The event_type passed by FUN_004DAA10 is event_type-3 from the ring buffer entry, but the encoding is likely a per-Element internal event ID, not raw packet opcode. Resolution requires identifying the queue producer (writers to zone+0x14/+0x18) to see what event_type is written - deferred to the async-queue-producer follow-up.

slot8_implementations.name: RaptureElement_primary_subobj_default_slot8_helper_FUN_0091C520
slot8_implementations.interpretation: Primary subobject default. Walks DAT_01357024-rooted linked list checking if param_1 matches a node by stepping through *(node+0x60). Returns 1 if found, 0 otherwise. Not an opcode dispatcher - this is a base-class state query helper inherited by 23 Element classes' primary vtables

slot8_implementations.name: Element_secondary_subobj_default_slot8_noop_FUN_00A72A20
slot8_implementations.interpretation: Secondary subobject (MI base) default. Just returns. 13 Element subclasses have NO per-class async opcode handler at vtable[8] and inherit this no-op

slot8_implementations.name: Element_bit0_flip_helper_FUN_0091C3E0
slot8_implementations.interpretation: Tiny: *(this+0x70) bit 0 = param_2 & 1. Called by 6 sites including FUN_004dab50 (RaptureElement::ctor). Used at TargetElement primary slot 8 and WidgetElement secondary slot 8, but NOT a Pattern B dispatcher - just inherited helper

slot8_implementations.name: CharaElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_0058E0C0
slot8_implementations.interpretation: CharaElement's Pattern B async tier opcode dispatcher. Largest of the 10 per-class slot-8 fns. Cases write payload to CharaElement state fields (+0x224, +0x244, +0x9C, +0xa4, etc.), trigger animations, send outgoing packets (case 0x51 calls FUN_004d6d10 with opcode 0xCA). Also calls FUN_0058F100, FUN_005852C0, FUN_00574A90, FUN_004D6750, FUN_004D7490, FUN_00585800, FUN_00587370, FUN_005901D0, FUN_0058DBE0, FUN_0058DE90, FUN_0058BC50, FUN_00585D10, FUN_0059E010, FUN_005854E0, FUN_00575260, FUN_004D6790, FUN_00587880, FUN_004D7390, FUN_0058EF40, FUN_0058F060 - the per-case handlers

slot8_implementations.name: MapLayoutElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_0059E660
slot8_implementations.interpretation: MapLayoutElement's Pattern B async tier. Cases 0x22 calls FUN_0059E530 (map-level routing); cases 0x23..0x28 share FUN_0059E300; case 0x2B sets *(this+0xB8)=1; case 0x2C sets *(this+0xB9)=*param_3

slot8_implementations.name: CutManagerElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_00566740
slot8_implementations.interpretation: CutManagerElement (cutscene manager) Pattern B async tier. 10 cutscene event types routing to FUN_00563D70 (case 4), FUN_005671E0+FUN_00565910 (case 5), FUN_0055D990 (case 6), FUN_005656E0 (case 7), FUN_005692F0 (case 8), FUN_00565760 (case 9), FUN_00569200+FUN_00564600 (case 10), FUN_0055FCB0 (case 0xB), FUN_0055FCE0 (case 0xC), FUN_0055FD00 (case 0xD). This confirms the Cut::* family was misnamed - the actual class is Application::Main::Element::System::CutManagerElement

slot8_implementations.name: CameraElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_0055EFD0
slot8_implementations.interpretation: CameraElement Pattern B async tier. Case 0x13 sets *(this+0x184)=*param_3 (camera mode?); case 0x15 calls FUN_00419B60 directly; case 0x16 sets *(this+0x124), calls FUN_0042FDC0 then FUN_00419B60; case 0x2E sets *(this+0x128) and *(this+0x138) (camera target positions)

slot8_implementations.name: ScreenshotManagerElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_00561440
slot8_implementations.interpretation: ScreenshotManagerElement Pattern B async tier. Only handles event 2 with branch on *param_3==1 vs other. Manipulates state fields +0x1B0, +0x1B1, +0x1B4, +0x1A4 (screenshot capture mode toggles)

slot8_implementations.name: GameManagerElement_async_event_dispatcher_slot8_FUN_0055DA80
slot8_implementations.interpretation: GameManagerElement Pattern B async tier. Tiny: case 0x19 sets *(this+0x244)=0, case 0x1A sets *(this+0x245)=0 (probably loading flags or game mode toggles)

slot8_implementations.interpretation: SqwtElement (UI shell) Pattern B async tier. Only handles event 0x2A: instantiates Sqwt::RoutedEventArgs on stack (with vftable from data), then calls FUN_0091E1C0 (the UI event router). Pattern B can therefore feed UI routed events too
